signaling_summary: NVMe Base 1.4 is a register-level protocol spec layered on top of PCI Express. All electrical signaling — transmitter equalization, receiver equalization, lane training, differential voltage, eye masks — is defined by the underlying PCI Express Base Specification (Gen 1 / 2 / 3 / 4) and the form-factor specifications (U.2, M.2, EDSFF E1.S / E3.S, AIC). The NVMe spec itself does not specify any analog parameter.

transport_signaling_references.purpose: All physical-layer signaling — encoding (8b/10b for Gen 1/2; 128b/130b for Gen 3+), differential voltage, return loss, jitter, lane equalization.
M.2 form-factor pin assignment and signaling.
E1.S / E3.S enterprise & data center form factors.

voltage_classes_via_pcie_formfactor.description: Standard PCIe slot/connector supply for storage form factors.
Primary supply for higher-power enterprise SSDs.

internal_analog_blocks_out_of_scope: The NVMe controller IP internally requires PCIe SerDes PHY (analog), reference clock buffer, PLLs, charge-pump regulators, and on-die NAND charge-pump / sense amplifiers for the storage media. None of these are specified by NVMe Base 1.4 — they are vendor / silicon implementation details, governed by the PCIe PHY specs (CEM/SFF connectors), the silicon process node's analog design kit, and the NAND / persistent-memory media's electrical interface (e.g. ONFI / Toggle DDR for NAND).
notes: Because NVMe Base 1.4 is a software-visible protocol/register specification, it does not contain any analog parameter tables. The spec is intentionally above the analog/digital boundary — all signaling is delegated to the underlying transport (PCIe) and its form factor.
